hero.line2: I study how people experience emerging technologies — building interactive prototypes and running mixed-methods user studies to understand what works and why.

paragraphs: I am an M.F.A. candidate at Jiangnan University School of Design, advised by Prof. Feng Wang. My research sits at the intersection of human-AI interaction, immersive media, and accessibility. I build interactive prototypes — Unity AR apps, TouchDesigner installations, Figma interfaces — and evaluate them through surveys, interviews, and structural equation models. My thesis explored how AR can support cultural heritage experiences (N=388, CB-SEM), and I am currently developing a PRISMA-based systematic review on generative AI for accessibility, screening 3,570 papers and coding 136 of them. I came to research through design: my B.F.A. taught me to care about how things look and feel, and my M.F.A. taught me to care about whether they actually work. Outside of work, I design typefaces, take too many photos, and have strong opinions about museum exhibition design.
about.highlight: I am currently looking for a summer 2026 research internship — especially projects in human-AI interaction, accessibility, AI-mediated communication, or immersive cultural interaction. If your lab needs someone who can prototype and run rigorous user studies, I would love to chat.

projects.title: REMEMBERY
projects.subtitle: Multi-Stakeholder Alzheimer's Care App
projects.cardBlurb: UX design across four user groups — patients, family caregivers, doctors, and social workers. Accessibility-first approach to cognitive decline and care coordination.
projects.description: A mobile application co-designed for four user groups within the Alzheimer's care ecosystem: patients managing cognitive decline, family caregivers coordinating daily support, doctors tracking clinical progress, and social workers allocating community resources. The design process began with stakeholder interviews and persona development to map the distinct needs of each group. For patients, the interface prioritizes simplified navigation, high-contrast visuals, and cognitive training exercises. For caregivers, it surfaces emergency workflows and care coordination tools. For clinicians, it provides a monitoring dashboard. For social workers, it supports case management and resource matching. Accessibility was not retrofitted — WCAG guidelines informed every wireframe from the start, shaping decisions about font sizing, touch targets, color contrast, and navigation hierarchy. The project demonstrates a complete user-centered design process from needs assessment through iterative prototyping to high-fidelity interactive mockups.

projects.title: NUA Museum
projects.subtitle: Website UX Redesign for University Museum
projects.cardBlurb: Heuristic evaluation + task analysis + IA redesign for Nanjing University of the Arts museum website. Structured around visitor goals.
projects.description: A comprehensive UX redesign for the Nanjing University of the Arts museum website. The project began with a heuristic evaluation identifying pain points in content discovery, navigation clarity, and visual hierarchy. Visitor task analysis — based on observing how students, faculty, and external visitors used the site — revealed that key functions like exhibition browsing, event registration, and collection exploration were buried under unclear navigation paths. The redesigned information architecture restructured content around three primary visitor goals. A visual refresh updated typography, color palette, and spacing while maintaining the institution's brand identity. The project demonstrates applied UX methodology in a real-world cultural institution context: from diagnostic evaluation through structural redesign to visual implementation.
projects.tools: Figma · Heuristic Evaluation · Task Analysis · Information Architecture · Visual Design

projects.title: 木上生画
projects.subtitle: Gamified Cultural Heritage EdTech App
projects.cardBlurb: iPad app for exploring traditional woodblock print heritage. Full UX process from card-sorting to high-fidelity interactive prototype.
projects.description: An iPad application designed to teach the centuries-old craft of Zhuxianzhen woodblock printing through interactive, gamified learning. The UX process followed a structured methodology: card-sorting exercises to define the information architecture, low-fidelity wireframes for rapid concept validation, and high-fidelity interactive prototypes built in Adobe XD. The app organizes content across three learning modules: History Tracing explores the origins and evolution of woodblock printing across Chinese dynasties; Craft Techniques demonstrates the step-by-step production process through interactive animations; and Proverb Games transforms traditional folk sayings into playful matching and puzzle challenges. The project demonstrates how structured UX research methods — from information architecture to prototyping — can transform passive cultural consumption into active, self-directed discovery.
projects.tools: Adobe XD · Card Sorting · Information Architecture · Wireframing · High-Fidelity Prototyping

projects.title: 敦煌奇妙夜
projects.subtitle: Immersive Heritage Installation with Physical Computing
projects.cardBlurb: Flashlight-driven immersive installation exploring Dunhuang murals. TouchDesigner + real-time 3D animation triggered by visitor interaction.
projects.description: This project aims to create a dynamic, immersive, and participatory exhibition experience by integrating historical art with contemporary interactive technology. It presents an immersive installation themed around Dunhuang culture, transforming traditional cultural imagery into an interactive spatial experience. In this work, visitors are invited to enter a virtual Dunhuang cave constructed through projection and 3D modeling. The mural figures and traditional Dunhuang musical instruments within the cave are reactivated as interactive elements awaiting exploration. Visitors hold infrared flashlights, and when the beam illuminates a figure on the mural, the corresponding character appears to be awakened and begins to play their instrument. At the same time, the sound of that instrument is triggered within the space, creating an immersive experience that combines visual perception, auditory feedback, and bodily interaction. The installation supports multi-user participation, allowing visitors to collaboratively activate different figures and instruments, collectively creating a unique Dunhuang-inspired visual and musical performance. The core concept of this work is to use digital technology to bridge the temporal and spatial distance between ancient cultural heritage and contemporary audiences. Through the interaction mechanism of illumination, awakening, and performance, visitors are no longer passive observers of the mural, but active participants in the reactivation of Dunhuang art. Each triggered beam of light symbolizes the renewal and continuation of traditional culture within a contemporary context.
projects.tools: TouchDesigner · Blender · Projection Mapping · Webcam Tracking · Physical Construction

projects.title: 宜兴紫砂 AR
projects.subtitle: AR Display Design for Cultural Heritage & User Acceptance
projects.cardBlurb: Mobile AR application for Yixing Zisha pottery. Unity + Vuforia prototype, N=388 CB-SEM evaluation — M.F.A. thesis project.
projects.description: A mobile AR application designed as my M.F.A. thesis project, exploring how augmented reality can bring traditional Yixing Zisha pottery craftsmanship to museum visitors. The prototype covers three modules: pot form knowledge, clay material comparison, and craftsmanship display. Built with Unity and Vuforia SDK. Evaluated through a CB-SEM study (N=388, SOR-TAM-Flow model) that identified perceived authenticity as the strongest driver of visitor engagement.
projects.tools: Unity · Vuforia SDK · CB-SEM (AMOS) · Mixed Methods · Prototyping
